documentation.reason: Retains the selected plumbing-only smoke design; it is excluded from paired dataset membership and was not executed.

purpose: Plumbing-only proof of custom Agent deployment, best-effort one-second metric collection, measured normal-backend timestamp survival, and fine-interval Bits querying.

app.name: pharmacy-replicaepoch-store
app.episode_description: Prescription readback serves an epoch older than the committed dispense authority.

selection_rationale.app_local_datadog_dependency: chart/Chart.yaml uses Datadog chart 3.82.0 guarded by datadog.enabled
selection_rationale.bounded_topology: pharmacy API, PostgreSQL, and continuous Locust ingress workload
selection_rationale.fault_mechanism: single application-control pod exec with explicit cleanup
selection_rationale.continuous_workload: 12 default Locust users, constant 0.5 second wait, dispense task weight 4 of 7
selection_rationale.expected_dogstatsd_timing_samples: well above one timing sample per second while dispenses continue

primary_fixture.producer_type: smoke-only Agent custom check injected through app-local Helm values
primary_fixture.collection_interval: requested 1s; surviving integer-second backend resolution is measured rather than normalized
primary_fixture.value_contract: monotonically increasing integer sequence used to quantify emitted points, duplicate wire timestamps, and backend-surviving points

ordinary_dogstatsd_fixture.client_aggregation: The app calls statsd.New without extended aggregation. Datadog-go v5.6.0 default client aggregation covers gauges, counts, and sets; extended aggregation is false, so timing samples are sent to the Agent without timing aggregation.

metric_contract.secondary_metric_note: Gauge is useful for scenario state but is not a one-second proof because default client-side gauge aggregation flushes every two seconds.

pharmacy_app_wiring.smoke_check: metric_resolution_smoke.py plus metric_resolution_smoke.yaml; smoke_run_id derives from runtime DD_ENV and the Agent supplies the canonical env tag
pharmacy_app_wiring.rendered_configmap_validation: passed for NTP exclusion, confd, and checksd
pharmacy_app_wiring.repository_syntax_validation: all executed checks passed except ShellCheck could not run because the executable is unavailable
pharmacy_app_wiring.limitations: Static render only; no native amd64 pull, PodSpec/imageID read-back, Agent status, backend, archival, Scenario Store, or Bits proof. SHARED_DATADOG_MODE=false remains a managed launch environment requirement rather than a chart value.

local_runtime_preflight.sink: local HTTP server accepting and decoding zlib-compressed v1 series payloads
local_runtime_preflight.scheduled_check_proof: cpu and uptime logged a 1s scheduler interval; system.cpu.user had 11 and system.uptime had 12 consecutive one-second timestamps
local_runtime_preflight.ordinary_dogstatsd_proof: gauge, count, and timing-derived series had distinct one-second timestamps and interval 1
local_runtime_preflight.timestamped_dogstatsd_proof: three exact producer timestamp/value pairs survived with interval 10
local_runtime_preflight.limitations: This is a local v1 JSON intake sink, not fakeintake, a packaged container, the normal metrics backend, or Bits. The local development build lacked installed datadog_checks Python dependencies, so the scheduled-check runtime proof used built-in core cpu and uptime checks rather than the smoke-only Python check.

local_kubernetes_preflight.control_proof: custom, cpu, and uptime checks retained 15-second cadence; ordinary DogStatsD gauge, count, and timing series retained interval 10 and ten-second timestamp gaps
local_kubernetes_preflight.treatment_proof: custom, cpu, and uptime checks plus ordinary DogStatsD gauge, count, and timing series each produced 20 distinct timestamps with one-second median gaps
local_kubernetes_preflight.timestamped_dogstatsd_proof: both arms preserved values 900, 901, and 902 with producer timestamp spacing and interval 10
local_kubernetes_preflight.pod_proof: both Agent pods were ready with zero restarts; PodSpec image and imageID matched the immutable digest and effective toggles differed as intended
local_kubernetes_preflight.limitations: Local arm64 Kubernetes and decoding intake proof only; not native amd64, fakeintake, normal metrics backend, Bits, managed GenSim, or a resource soak. Non-metric event-platform requests produced expected errors with placeholder credentials before the scenario was hardened to disable those collectors.

merge_head_packaged_runtime_preflight.control_proof: ordinary DogStatsD gauge, count, and timing-derived series retained interval 10 and ten-second timestamp gaps
merge_head_packaged_runtime_preflight.treatment_proof: ordinary DogStatsD and smoke-check series had one-second median timestamp gaps; treatment serializer request cadence had a 0.999-second median gap
merge_head_packaged_runtime_preflight.timestamped_dogstatsd_proof: both arms preserved values 900, 901, and 902 with exact producer timestamps and interval 10
merge_head_packaged_runtime_preflight.limitations: Native arm64 packaged-container and local decoding-intake proof only; the merge-head digest still needs Kubernetes soak, native amd64 managed deployment, normal-backend, and Bits proof.

merge_head_local_kubernetes_soak.control_cadence: ordinary DogStatsD 10 seconds; smoke, cpu, and uptime checks 15 seconds
merge_head_local_kubernetes_soak.treatment_cadence: 921 consecutive one-second timestamps for ordinary DogStatsD count, gauge, timing average, smoke sequence, cpu user, and uptime across the measured window plus flush settling
merge_head_local_kubernetes_soak.timestamped_dogstatsd: values 900, 901, and 902 preserved with interval 10 in both arms

slow_check_completion.kubernetes_apiserver: 328 executions across approximately 900 effective one-second scheduler intervals; average execution 2014 ms
slow_check_completion.ntp: 764 executions across approximately 900 effective one-second scheduler intervals; average execution 537 ms. The check's default 900-second interval explicitly follows pool.ntp.org query-rate guidance, so globally forcing it toward one second is a deployment safety blocker regardless of overlap skips.

merge_head_local_kubernetes_soak.skip_probe: a separate 30-second post-soak DEBUG probe observed 18 kubernetes_apiserver skips and 6 ntp skips; it is excluded from resource measurements
merge_head_local_kubernetes_soak.queue_lag: not a gate for same-check overlap: the pre-existing worker guard immediately discards a tick when that check ID is already running rather than queueing it
merge_head_local_kubernetes_soak.overlap_skip_acceptance: accepted as pre-existing Agent behavior; do not change pkg/collector/worker/worker.go
merge_head_local_kubernetes_soak.resource_thresholds: not required by the experiment owner; CPU and RSS remain informational observations
merge_head_local_kubernetes_soak.follow_up: This soak established the NTP risk. A later focused validation rejected empty ntp.yaml as ineffective and proved supported suppression with integration.excluded: [ntp]. NTP safety is locally resolved. Check-generated timestamp collisions are now a measured best-effort outcome rather than a managed-deployment blocker.
merge_head_local_kubernetes_soak.limitations: Local native-arm64 Kubernetes and decoding-intake evidence only; not native amd64, normal-backend, Bits, or managed GenSim proof.

merge_head_ntp_suppression_validation.matched_configuration: agents.customAgentConfig.integration.excluded contains only ntp in both arms; scenarios otherwise differ only by DD_METRIC_RESOLUTION_EXPERIMENT_ENABLED
merge_head_ntp_suppression_validation.rejected_approach: an empty regular ntp.yaml produced a no-valid-instances error and did not suppress ntp.d/conf.yaml.default
merge_head_ntp_suppression_validation.ntp_suppression: passed in control and treatment; NTP was absent from runner status and the effective integration.excluded configuration was mounted
merge_head_ntp_suppression_validation.public_ntp_request_evidence: No NTP check code path was scheduled after exclusion; direct packet capture was not performed.
merge_head_ntp_suppression_validation.control_cadence: passed with 10-second ordinary DogStatsD and 15-second smoke, cpu, and uptime cadence without internal gaps
merge_head_ntp_suppression_validation.treatment_dogstatsd: passed a clean capture with 96 distinct one-second count, gauge, and timing-average timestamps
merge_head_ntp_suppression_validation.treatment_uptime: passed a clean capture with 96 distinct one-second timestamps
merge_head_ntp_suppression_validation.treatment_smoke_sequence: best-effort baseline: 96 emitted points, 67 distinct timestamps, and 29 duplicate timestamp assignments (30.2% at risk of same-timestamp backend deduplication)
merge_head_ntp_suppression_validation.treatment_cpu_user: best-effort baseline: 96 emitted points, 83 distinct timestamps, and 13 duplicate timestamp assignments (13.5% at risk of same-timestamp backend deduplication)
merge_head_ntp_suppression_validation.acceptance: Proceed to the managed smoke without timestamp normalization. Measure emitted sequence count, duplicate wire timestamps, backend-surviving points, and effective spacing per metric. Known same-context integer-second collisions are acceptable when quantified; stop on missing metrics, timestamp rewriting, or loss not explained by those collisions.
merge_head_ntp_suppression_validation.limitations: Local native-arm64 Kubernetes and decoding-intake evidence only; not native amd64, normal-backend, Bits, or managed GenSim proof.

gs_admin_sync_plan.group_evidence: No existing Pharmacy identity was found; all 25 existing staging episodes tagged gensim-apps.source=gensim-apps belong to group gensim.

pass_gates: Running Agent PodSpec image uses the selected repository and digest.
Running Pod imageID resolves to the same immutable digest.
Filtered agent config and agent status prove the effective one-second experiment settings.
The smoke-only custom check emits the exact monotonic sequence for 60-120 seconds without serializer errors.
Pharmacy timing samples arrive without sustained DogStatsD drops or serializer errors.
Direct normal-backend queries quantify emitted sequence values, duplicate integer-second timestamps, backend-surviving values, ordering, and exact execution tags for metric_resolution.smoke.sequence.
Direct normal-backend queries discover the emitted pharmacy timing-series names and show materially finer treatment resolution than control for at least one timing series.
Returned treatment losses are limited to measured same-context integer-second collisions; any additional loss is explained or stops the smoke.
Managed archival and Scenario Store projection complete for the same execution.
Bits queries the same org, tags, and historical window with an interval fine enough to return the one-second points.
The Bits trace records the metric request, requested interval or rollup, returned timestamp spacing, and use of metric evidence.
No interpolation, timestamp rewriting, wrong-scope query, unexplained point loss, restart, or OOM occurs.
stop_conditions: Custom image or effective config cannot be proven from the running workload.
The custom check does not run continuously, its surviving backend resolution is not materially finer than control, or the pharmacy producer emits too few timing samples to compare arms.
The normal backend returns only coarse points despite a fine query interval, or loses points beyond measured same-context integer-second collisions.
Bits requests or receives a coarse rollup.
The telemetry org, tags, or incident window do not match the managed execution.
Managed archival or Scenario Store lineage is incomplete.
